segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Do not speak harshly to an older man, but appeal to him as a father, to younger men as brothers,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: to older women as mothers, to younger women as sisters, in all purity.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Honor widows who are truly widows.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But if any widow has children or grandchildren, let them first learn to show devotion to their own household and to repay their parents and grandparents, for this is acceptable before God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The one who is truly a widow, left all alone, has set her hope on God and continues in petitions and prayers night and day;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: but the one who lives for pleasure is dead while she lives.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Command these things as well, so that they may be above reproach.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But if anyone does not provide for their own people, and especially for members of their household, they have denied the faith and are worse than an unbeliever.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Let a widow be enrolled if she is not less than sixty years old, the wife of one husband,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: well attested for good works: if she has raised children, if she has shown hospitality to strangers, if she has washed the feet of holy ones, if she has helped those in distress, if she has devoted herself to every good work.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But decline younger widows; for when their desires draw them away from Christ, they want to marry,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and so they incur judgment, because they have set aside their first pledge.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At the same time they also learn to be idle, going around from house to house, and not only idle but also gossips and busybodies, saying things they should not.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So I want the younger ones to marry, bear children, manage their households, and give the adversary no opening for abuse.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For some have already turned aside to follow Satan.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: If any believing woman has widows in her family, let her help them, and let the assembly not be burdened, so that it can help those who are truly widows.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Let the elders who lead well be considered worthy of double honor, especially those who labor in preaching and teaching;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for the Scripture says,

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “You shall not muzzle an ox while it is threshing,”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and,

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “The worker is worthy of his wages.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Do not accept an accusation against an elder unless it rests on two or three witnesses.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Those who persist in sinning, reprove in front of everyone, so that the rest also may be afraid.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I solemnly charge you before God and Christ Jesus and the chosen angels to keep these things without prejudgment, doing nothing out of partiality.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Do not be quick to lay hands on anyone, and do not share in the sins of others; keep yourself pure.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Stop drinking only water, and use a little wine for the sake of your stomach and your frequent illnesses.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The sins of some people are plain to see, going ahead of them to judgment; but those of others follow after them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In the same way good works too are plain to see, and even those that are not cannot stay hidden.

notes.traditional: an elder (KJV); an older man (most modern versions)
notes.note: The Greek word means both an older man and an elder who holds office in the community. Here it is paired with younger men, older women and younger women, so age is meant. In verses 17 and 19 the same word refers to the office and is rendered 'elder'.

In this passage 'honor' includes material support, not only respect. The following verses concern who should provide for widows, and the related noun in verse 17 is connected with a worker's wages. The word echoes the commandment to honor father and mother, which was understood to include caring for them in old age.

The verb describes fulfilling one's sacred duty, and was used of dutiful conduct toward parents and family as well as toward the gods. 'Godliness' now suggests private religious feeling, whereas the point here is a religious obligation discharged by caring for one's own family.

notes.traditional: be enrolled / be put on the list
notes.note: The verb means to enter someone on an official list. The community evidently kept a register of widows. It is debated whether this was simply a list of those entitled to support or a recognised group who also had duties of prayer and service; verses 11–12 suggest that enrollment involved some kind of commitment.

Literally 'a woman of one man'. It may mean she was married only once, an ideal praised in ancient epitaphs, or that she was faithful to her husband during the marriage. Since verse 14 urges younger widows to remarry, many interpreters prefer the second reading, but the question is not settled.

The word refers to all members of the believing community as people set apart for God, echoing the Septuagint's language for Israel. 'Saints' now suggests canonised individuals or people of exceptional virtue, which is not meant here. Many translations keep 'saints'; others use 'God's people'.

notes.phrase: their desires draw them away from Christ
notes.traditional: wax wanton against Christ / their passions draw them away from Christ
notes.note: The verb occurs only here in the New Testament and is very rare elsewhere. The simpler related verb means to live in sensual indulgence, and the compound adds the idea of doing so against someone. The sense appears to be that strong desires, probably sexual, set them at odds with their commitment to Christ; the precise nuance is uncertain.

The word usually rendered 'faith' also meant a pledge or solemn promise, and with the verb used here ('set aside, annul') it formed a recognised idiom for breaking one's word. The reference is probably to a commitment made on enrollment, perhaps to remain unmarried in Christ's service. The traditional rendering 'their first faith' is possible, but it would imply that remarriage is itself an abandonment of the faith, which verse 14 contradicts.

notes.traditional: any man or woman that believeth (KJV)
notes.note: The earliest manuscripts read 'any believing woman'. Many later manuscripts read 'any believing man or woman', and that longer form lies behind the King James Version. It is generally thought that scribes expanded the text because it seemed odd to limit the duty to women. The shorter reading is followed here.

The Greek word was the ordinary term for a civic gathering and the Septuagint's word for Israel assembled. 'Church' now suggests a building or an institution, so this translation uses 'assembly' throughout. 'Church' is the near-universal rendering, and readers will recognise that the same community is meant.

The Greek word means both honor and a price or payment, and could be used of an honorarium. The quotations about the ox and the worker's wages in the next verse show that material support is at least included. Whether 'double' means twice the pay of others, or respect together with pay, or simply generous provision, is disputed.

notes.phrase: “The worker is worthy of his wages.”
notes.traditional: The labourer is worthy of his reward / deserves his wages
notes.note: The first quotation is Deuteronomy 25:4. The second is not found in the Jewish Scriptures; it matches word for word a saying of Jesus in Luke 10:7. Whether the author cites a written Gospel as Scripture, or the phrase 'the Scripture says' strictly covers only the first quotation with a well-known saying added, is debated.

Laying on of hands was the gesture by which someone was commissioned for a role in the community (see 4:14). In this context about elders, the warning is most likely against appointing someone to office too hastily and so sharing responsibility for that person's later failings. A minority view takes it as the readmission of a disciplined offender.

candidates.reason: The word group is central to the Pastoral Letters and 2 Peter, and translations vary between godliness, piety, religion and devotion; it needs one decision covering noun, verb and adjective.
The split between age and office recurs across the Gospels, Acts, the letters and Revelation, and readers should see a consistent pair of renderings.
Translations vary between rebuke, reprove, convict and expose across John, the Pastorals, Ephesians and Revelation, and it needs to be kept distinct from ἐπιτιμάω and ἐπιπλήσσω.
It is rendered variously as judgment, condemnation or damnation across the New Testament, and needs distinguishing from κρίσις (v. 24) and κατάκριμα.
The word covers both honor and price or payment; a policy is needed for passages where material support is in view (here, and the verb in v. 3).
